back: Usually a person/group; comes before the DO (e.g., 'bring me some milk') [17].
Usually a thing; comes after the IO [17].
Reversing order using 'to' or 'for' before the IO (e.g., 'pass that to me') [17].
Use the prepositional pattern if the IO is much longer than the DO [17].
If DO is a pronoun, the pattern 'DO + prep + IO' is required (e.g., 'give it to me') [17].
Suggests someone benefits (e.g., 'wrote a letter for her' because she couldn't) [17].
Suggests transfer/communication (e.g., 'wrote a letter to her') [17].
Verbs like envy, allow, ask, cost cannot have objects reversed with 'to'/'for' [17].
Verbs like describe, fix, collect, mend only take a second object as a prep object [17].
